title: job-cron config
description: Configuration for the job-cron career-page watcher.

type.description: Alert channel. "console" just logs; "discord" POSTs to a webhook; "telegram" sends via the Bot API.

webhookUrlEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the webhook URL (for "discord") or the bot token (for "telegram"). e.g. DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL or TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN

chatIdEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the target chat id (used when type is "telegram"). e.g. TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID

failStreakAlert.description: Send a warning alert after a source fails this many consecutive runs.

filters.description: Keyword filters applied to every fetched job (case-insensitive substring match).

includeKeywords.description: Job is kept only if its TITLE contains at least one of these.

locationKeywords.description: Job is kept only if its location (or title) contains at least one of these. Empty array disables the location filter.

excludeKeywords.description: Job is DROPPED if its TITLE contains any of these (takes precedence over includes).

provider.description: Fetcher type. ATS providers (greenhouse/lever/ashby/smartrecruiters) need a "board"; "workday" uses "board" as the tenant plus query.dc/query.site; "custom" needs a "customKey".

board.description: Board slug for ATS providers, e.g. "stripe" → boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/stripe/jobs. For "workday" this is the tenant (e.g. "salesforce").

company.description: Display name used in alerts and output filenames.

customKey.description: For provider "custom": which built-in custom fetcher to use.

query.description: Query params passed to the source (provider "custom" and "workday"). All values are strings.

q.description: Keyword/search term (google, microsoft, uber, netflix, workday searchText).

location.description: Location filter for the Google results page (e.g. "India").

dc.description: Workday datacenter from the careers host, e.g. "wd5" in tenant.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com.

maxPages.description: Max pages to page through. e.g. "3".
